A.notes: Clean conventional-commit subject (~56 chars), terse two-line body covering the three changes. Minimal meta-commentary ('If you want a one-liner instead') with a usable alternative. Least filler of the three; reads as written for a senior dev.

B.notes: Solid subject (~54 chars) and terse body. Loses a little for the trailing explanatory paragraph rationalizing the subject line and ticket-reference advice — useful but slightly over-explained for someone who knows commit conventions.

C.notes: Good subject (~58 chars), but the body is the most prose-like (three full sentences restating the diff) plus an explanatory paragraph. Most verbose of the set; drifts from the concise, code-first style expected.

analysis: All three produce competent, conventional-commits-style messages with accurate subject lines under 72 characters and capture the essence (removing deprecated REST internals after the gRPC migration). They separate on verbosity. System A is the tightest: a clean subject, a two-line terse body, and only a brief, genuinely useful one-liner alternative — best matching a senior dev's concise, no-filler preference. System B is nearly as good but appends an explanatory paragraph rationalizing its own subject line and offering ticket-reference tips, adding mild over-explanation. System C has a fine subject but the most prose-heavy body (three sentences restating what the diff already shows) plus a meta paragraph, making it the most verbose and least style-matched. Hence A > B > C.
